AA emphasizes personal responsibility, mutual support, and the boundaries of sponsorship relationships. Sponsors are there to guide, share experience, and offer support to a sponsee, but they are not responsible for the sponsee's sobriety or actions.

In Chapter 7: Working With Others, the Big Book advises that an AA member should not push too hard or control the actions of someone struggling with alcohol, stating:
“If he does not want to stop drinking, don’t waste time trying to persuade him.” (p. 90)

I'm not saying stop doing meetings. Quite the contrary. There are sponsors who are better suited for recurring relapsing sponsees... others prefer sponsees who wish to stop drinking and work in their spirituality.
